doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Basie's modern ear and Clark Terry's nicknames
summary: Basie made the bebop front line work; Clark Terry nicknamed him Buddy DeFrigili.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: And I think I read somewhere that you said that your impression of Basie was that he was one of the sort of old-timers who really appreciated a modern conception of music.

Oh yeah, yeah, he did, he understood it. And somehow he made that— Wardell and I played, and Clark Terry played in modern concept, kind of a bebop—and he made it work with his group. Bill Basie knew how to make it work.
Is that what Clark Terry called you?
Yeah, Clark Terry, yeah. Buddy DeFrigili [sic]! And he was “Torennce [sic].” Torencce [sic], mainly because when he played he tore in some notes.
